candidates.sentence: I will continue to advocate for further action to ensure that our Southern and Northern borders are secure, deploy technology and crack down on the trafficking of deadly substances like fentanyl, and address the deficiencies in our laws.

And as we work to lower the deficit and ensure the biggest corporations pay their fair share, I won’t support any legislation that increases taxes on those making less than $400,000 a year while working to ensure our small businesses have the incentives they need to succeed.

I’ve helped secure more than $40 million in federal funding to help strengthen our stock of affordable housing, and I am fighting to expand the Low Income Housing Tax Credit which will allow for more development.
Throughout my time in Congress, I have pushed for greater funding that will provide security at our border and legislation that will fix our broken immigration system.
I’m fighting for bipartisan, commonsense solutions to lower taxes and cut costs for small businesses and working families.
We must expand the Child Tax Credit to put more money back in the pockets of hard-working families and tackle the affordable housing crisis that New Hampshire is facing.
I’ll keep fighting to restore reproductive freedom and stop extremists from turning back the clock on women’s rights.

As a member of the Veterans’ Affairs Committee, I’ve made advocating for veterans and their families a central priority of my time in Congress, and I’ll always fight to ensure our veterans receive the health care they need and the benefits they’ve earned.

My bill to ensure law enforcement can prevent deadly opioids from coming into our communities has become law, and I’ll keep fighting for resources to expand treatment and recovery and address New Hampshire’s addiction epidemic.
I’ll continue to fight for commonsense reforms to protect our communities from gun violence.
We need a system of legal immigration that supports our communities and economic future and adheres to our American values.
